operator.name: Steam Ship Sudan (Voyageurs du Monde)
operator.display_rule: Information only. Photos used with the operator's permission (Islam, 5 November 2026); six of the seven have digitally extended sides, which their captions say. Attribute the operator's own claims (launch year, the Agatha Christie connection, engineering).

propulsion_support.text: Its triple-expansion steam engine still turns the paddle wheels, now fired by diesel rather than coal, with an auxiliary thruster to help.

enquiry_partner.name: Original Travel
enquiry_partner.role: Takes enquiries for this ship. Not its operator.

deck_plan.note: Only a 2007 plan exists, with different cabin names and 21 units. Historical reference, not shown.

on_board.food: The operator describes a menu created with chef Jean Imbert around Egyptian ingredients such as Nile fish, lentils, spices, citrus and hibiscus.

wifi.value: Reported aboard, patchy on a January 2023 voyage

cabin_amenities.value: Air conditioning, internal telephone, safe, hairdryer, 220 V sockets (2024 report)

suitability.children: Children under six are not accepted.
suitability.less_suited_to: Families travelling with children under six.

fleet_defaults.route_note: From late November to mid-February, low water stops the ship sailing between Luxor and Qena, and an alternative programme applies. Abydos is visited by road.

cabin.name: Cabin
cabin.feature: Named and decorated individually, with two windows onto the shared promenade deck. Most are on the upper deck, the others on the main deck.

suite.name: Suite
suite.feature: Named and decorated individually, with larger panoramic windows. Three are at the prow and stern of the upper deck; the others are at the bow of the main deck, on the poop deck and on the sun deck, where the Odilo suite has a private deck.

vessels.name: Steam Ship Sudan

built_year.note: The operator's history ('Sudan ex machina'): launched in Cairo in 1921, its machinery shipped from Scotland. 1885 is when Cook's earlier steamer fleet was begun, not this hull (checked 6 November 2026).

renovated_year.note: The operator: a new engine in 1991, then 'in 2007 the ship went into dry dock for its first major round of renovation'. A further round planned for 2024 isn't confirmed as done.

vessels.summary: A historic side-wheel paddle steamer, launched in 1921 according to its operator, with 18 cabins and six suites across three decks.

deck_plan.note: Checked 5 November 2026: no deck plan found. The ship's cabin pages place 12 cabins on the upper deck and 4 on the main deck (2 not stated); suites: Agatha Christie and Lady Duff Gordon at the upper deck's prow, Queen Victoria at its stern, Oum Kalsoum across the main deck's bow, Aïda on the poop deck and Odilo on the sun deck. Ask the operator for a plan, the guest capacity and the length.

vessels.description: Every cabin and suite has its own name and decoration, from Agatha Christie to Naguib Mahfouz. Agatha Christie cruised the Nile in 1933, four years before Death on the Nile, and the ship’s operator identifies the Sudan as the steamer that inspired the novel.
